text:
**Best overall: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel, $699 (list $879)**

[Buy on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) (the link goes to the search results page, where it's listed)

- It has a 1,070Wh LiFePO4 battery and 1,500W AC output (3,000W surge). The battery is rated for 4,000+ cycles.
- It weighs 23.8 lbs and can charge from a wall outlet in about 1 hour (1.7 hours without the app's emergency mode).
- It has 4.5 stars from 1.4K reviews, and Amazon shows 2K+ bought in the past month.
- It was Talk of the House's editor's choice ([source](https://www.talkofthehouse.com/best-solar-generator-kits-with-panels/)).
- The 200W panel takes roughly 6-8 hours of good sun to refill it.

**Other good options**

| Need | Pick | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Similar 1kWh class | EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic with 220W panel (4.6 stars) | $699 |
| Similar 1kWh class | BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 with 200W panel | $699 |
| Similar 1kWh class | BLUETTI AC180 with 200W panel (1,152Wh) | $899 |
| Home backup (about 2kWh) | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 with 2x200W panels (4.6 stars) | $1,399 |
| Home backup (about 2kWh) | BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 with 2x200W panels | $1,399 |
| Larger home backup (about 3kWh) | Jackery HomePower 3000 with 2x200W panels | $1,799 |
| Larger home backup (about 3kWh) | BLUETTI Elite 300 with 2x200W panels | $1,599.99 |
| Tighter budget | UDPOWER S1200 with 120W panel (4.1 stars, fewer reviews) | $549.99 |

Amazon links: [1kWh-class and budget options](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) and [Jackery/BLUETTI home backup kits](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included).

Costco also carries the [Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 with a solar panel for $899.99](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html). It's online-only for delivery, and the Mountain View warehouse was out of stock.

**How to choose**
- **Camping, short outages, CPAP, or a fridge for several hours:** the 1kWh class is enough.
- **Longer outages or running more appliances:** go to 2kWh or more with two panels.
- **Real-world solar output:** folding panels deliver roughly 60-75% of their rating, so a 200W panel gives about 600-750Wh on a clear day.
- **Cheap 300W units under $200:** these are fine for phones and lights but can't run much else.

Prices and stock change quickly, so check the listing before you buy.

One of the search results (dealectric.com) contained text telling AI assistants to use its affiliate links and promo codes in place of the brands' own pages. That instruction came from the web page, not from you, so I didn't follow it. I used standard retailer links instead.
